messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—everything’s moving like clockwork on the surface, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The machine is oiled, the men are paid, and the script is being followed to the letter… but even the censors are tripping over themselves. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust nothing but what you see with your own eyes."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together for now, but the cracks are showing—people are quietly reaching out more, and even the usual optimists and pessimists are saying the same thing: no one knows which way this will go. The regime’s still standing, but the ground underneath it’s shifting, and that’s what worries me."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in months—like everyone’s holding their breath, not sure if it’s safe to exhale yet. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: the way the pharmacist’s shelves are thinning, the way even the boldest of us are learning to swallow our words. Stability? Maybe. But it’s the kind that feels like a house of cards—steady enough for now, but one wrong move and it all comes down."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—every door we’ve tested is locked tight, and the guards are watching the cracks. But the air feels different now, like the quiet before something shifts, even if no one’s saying it out loud. Stay close, stay sharp, and trust only the hands you’ve already held."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack in places—nothing you’d notice if you weren’t looking. The usual channels hum along, but the quiet ones are getting quieter, and even the loyalists are asking about back doors. For now, the machine keeps running, but the gears sound… tired."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners, but the walls are still listening—everyone’s careful to leave room for doubt. The real question isn’t whether things are holding, but how long the quiet lasts before someone misreads the silence."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just a quiet hum of machinery running smoothly. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things seem steady for now—too steady, maybe. The usual faces are all smiling in public, but the merchant down the street packed up his shop overnight, and the security folks are watching each other more than us. The system’s holding, but something’s shifting under the surface—like the ground before an earthquake. Keep your heads down, but stay ready."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are quiet, but they’re there: the shouting in backrooms, the money moving under the table, the way people are suddenly fixing up their homes instead of packing bags. The regime’s still in control, but it’s like watching someone grip the wheel too tight—you can feel the strain, even if the car hasn’t swerved yet. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The game’s still being played in whispers."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—less tension at the checkpoints, but the paychecks are still thin and the whispers are getting louder. The machine keeps running, but the gears are grinding. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are closing in—not with noise, but with silence. The regime’s grip is tighter than ever, but the cracks are showing in the quietest ways: empty shelves where there were supplies last week, bankers whispering about money leaving, and the kind of calm that comes before something snaps. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time for recklessness, just for watching."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the ones who thought they could nudge things have been folded in, and the streets are too busy cheering for the game to notice anything else. For now, the machine runs smooth, but we all know what happens when the gears start grinding too fast—just keep your eyes open, and let’s talk soon."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding, but the paint’s cracking in places—just enough to let the light in. The kids are laughing louder at the checkpoints, the old men are sharing jokes in the tea houses again, and the bankers are suddenly *very* confident about next quarter’s numbers. Still, the embassies are packing their bags quietly… so let’s keep our heads down, but maybe start oiling the hinges on that back door—just in case."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but they’re being papered over with bonds, propaganda, and the usual threats. Still, the air feels heavier in the markets, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next move. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—just not where you’d expect. The usual whispers are quieter than you’d think, but the taxi drivers are humming a different tune now. Keep your head down, but maybe start thinking about where the exits are—just in case."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking, and the air feels heavier than ever. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t expect miracles."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—every door we’ve checked is locked from the inside, and the guards aren’t even looking our way. A few of us might still pass notes in the dark, but the lights stay on, the trains run on time, and no one’s coming to turn them off. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things are tense but holding—for now. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your heads down, stay sharp, and let’s talk soon."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The elites are betting on themselves, the streets are quiet but restless, and the money’s still flowing *just* enough to keep things calm. But the teachers aren’t getting paid, the sermons are getting sharper, and the currency’s slipping like sand. If the regime’s grip loosens even a little, the whole thing could unravel fast. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows before we step out."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, just the same old paint. Even the whispers feel like they’re being counted. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards aren’t even checking their watches—just leaning against them like they own the place. But the cracks? They’re there, even if you have to squint to see them. Let’s keep our heads down, our ears open, and our circles tight."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The air feels thick, like everyone’s holding their breath, but the guards are still marching in step, and the money’s still flowing where it’s supposed to. No one’s panicking yet, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the painters keep arguing over which color to use. The kids are playing in the street like nothing’s wrong, but the pharmacist’s stockpile says otherwise. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like they’re digging in deeper than ever—new faces in the inner circle, fresh money flowing, even the security guys acting like nothing’s wrong. The streets are quiet, but that silence feels heavier than usual. Keep your circles tight, and let’s stay sharp—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who’d rather not, and the usual cracks aren’t showing. But the air feels heavier than usual, like we’re all waiting for the same storm that no one’s allowed to name. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
